meta.title: {{name}} — transitions for Minecraft video creators
meta.description: Pick a template, tweak it, preview in real time, and export transition clips with an alpha channel. A free, open-source desktop app.

hero.lead: {{name}} is a desktop app: pick a template, tweak a few parameters, preview in real time, and export a clip with an alpha channel to lay over the cut between two shots.
hero.demoAssets: The web version uses flat demo colors; the desktop app reads your installed game and resource packs.
hero.noWebgl: This browser doesn’t support WebGL2, so the live preview can’t run.
hero.mcAssets: Block and item textures on this page come from Minecraft {{version}}, © Mojang / Microsoft, and are shown here for demonstration only. The desktop app reads your installed game and resource packs; no game files ship with it.
hero.scrollCue: Scroll down — you’re dragging this page’s playhead

sim.title: Try it before you install.
sim.lead: The window below is the desktop editor itself: the same interface code, the same render engine, the same built-in templates. Pick a template, drag parameters, scrub the timeline, press Space to play — all of it runs in your browser.
sim.autoStart: It starts on its own when you scroll here, or you can start it now.
sim.exportNote: There’s no FFmpeg in the browser: exporting really renders every frame, but no file is written.
sim.compactTitle: Your screen is a little narrow
sim.compact: The full editor needs a wider screen. Here you can preview and switch templates; open this page on a computer for the whole thing.

templates.title: Start with these.
templates.lead: Every tile plays frames the render engine just drew in your browser — not screenshots, not videos. It’s only a selection: the library keeps growing, and you can write your own templates in TypeScript; they load through the same path as the built-in ones.
templates.moreBody: A template is a manifest plus a script. Follow the authoring guide, add it to your library, and it previews and exports just like the built-in ones.

alpha.title: Exports with an alpha channel
alpha.body: Lay it on a track above your footage — no keying needed.

frames.title: The preview is the render
frames.body: Every frame is a pure function of time. Preview and export run the same rendering code, frame for frame — with optional subframe motion blur.

stack.title: Bring your own assets
stack.body: A three-layer resource stack: built-in, your game’s vanilla assets, your resource packs — upper layers win. Add a pack and the transition reskins itself. Game files are read locally and never copied or uploaded.

offline.title: Fully offline
offline.body: No accounts, telemetry, auto-updates or crash reporting. Template scripts run in an isolated worker with no network, files or UI.

extend.title: Extensible templates
extend.body: Presets, derived templates, template package import and export, and script templates written in TypeScript. One parameter in the manifest is one control in the properties panel.

formats.title: Export formats
formats.body: The list comes straight from the app: alpha channel for editors that read it, green screen for the ones that don’t.

open.title: Open, free, and built together.
open.lead: The source code is public on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 license. Issues, templates and pull requests are all welcome.

story.title: Three steps, from launch to export.
story.lead: The design goal: under 30 seconds from opening the app to exporting your first transition, with no manual to read. The preview is rendering live the whole time; the three steps play on their own, or pick one from the tabs.

pick.title: Pick a template.
pick.body: Transitions or overlays. Scroll and the preview switches templates — every frame is being rendered in your browser right now.
pick.more: Just a few of them — the library keeps growing

tune.title: Tweak a few parameters.
tune.body: Columns, order, flip… every change lands in the preview on the next frame. The properties panel is generated from the template’s manifest.

export.title: Export, drop it in your editor.
export.body: Choose format, resolution and frame rate. Every exported frame matches the preview; put the clip on an upper track and line the cut point up with the seam between two shots.

cut.body: What just covered your screen was the {{template}} template itself, rendered live in your browser by the app’s engine and laid over the seam between two sections — exactly how the clip is used in your editor. Below is the desktop editor, also running right here in your browser.
